initial_conditions: An empty release studio on Debian 13.7 ARM64, a headless Sway Wayland output, the GTK file chooser, two original SVG fixtures and a single-hole editable pocket.
actions: Build the pinned unsigned release offline on Debian ARM64 and independently read every package file. Retain and recheck the earlier package.
Import the two-slot SVG into the empty studio through GTK. Undo and Redo. Save the project and export the rest OBJ and workspace PNG.

Open the saved project in a fresh studio. Move the upper-left point of the large slot 20 mm left. Save and export. Import the overlapping fixture and retain the refusal. Save again, clear and reopen the edited file.

In a third process, open the single-hole file and create the second rectangular hole in the inspector at (15, 20) mm with a size of 30 × 40 mm. Apply, save, export, Undo, Redo and save. Close all test processes and shut down the guest.
Run python3 -B parity/reports/artifacts/debian-wayland-multiple-cutouts-20261120/replay.py to compare each saved field, the exported geometry and the retained package and display records.
expected_outcomes: Undo and Redo restore the empty and imported states. Moving one corner preserves the other opening. Both OBJ meshes have three boundary loops and net areas of 0.0756 and 0.0744 m². A rejected overlap preserves the last editable bytes. Adding the second opening in the inspector preserves all prior IDs.
